quelle: G9c2: Sklavenhändler aus Arena Theory 1.0 (trader.js L, barracks.js WORDS/TIERS/analysis, besondere.js trader/BADGE, buy-odds.js NAMES/LINES), ins Englische übertragen. Wird erst geladen, wenn der Marktstand geöffnet wird. Schlüssel = deutscher 1.0-Text bzw. 1.0-Schlüssel.

odds.besser: You'd have got a better one in {p} % of cases.
human: Almost anyone would have been better. Even the corpse you buried yesterday.
A dolt. Next time you'll almost certainly get a better one. Worse is barely possible.
I've seen corpses with more talent. Rotted ones.
I wouldn't even use him as a battering ram. Battering rams have dignity.
Congratulations on the worst roll of the week. The arena sand is already looking forward to him.
Below average. He won't die faster than the others, just uglier.
More than half would have been better. But they weren't on offer.
He won't be a hero. But everyone deserves a tragic ending.
Solid cannon fodder. Emphasis on fodder.
Average. He'll die like most do: loudly and surprised.
Neither gold nor dung. Just meat with opinions.
Mediocre. The hall of the dead still has room for mediocre.
An honest roll. Honestly boring.
Decent. He might even survive his first fight. Might.
Better than most. Make sure the smith doesn't see him.
A usable roll. The gods only glanced over briefly.
Quite respectable. Almost a shame to let him die.
Good catch. You don't get one like this every day. Don't feed him to the lion right away.
That's a proper piece. Rare as a sober smith.
He has talent. That makes his death all the more expensive later.
Fortuna was merciful. Enjoy it, she holds grudges.
A rare piece! Only one in a hundred. The trader is weeping in secret now.
Rare. When he dies, he gets a bigger grave.
You won't find one like him again. So please don't throw him to the roosters straight away.
A jewel out of the muck. He just doesn't know it yet.
A lucky strike! One in a thousand. Sacrifice to Fortuna, or at least a recruit.
That's a miracle on two legs. For now. Watch his legs.
The gods rolled wrong. Keep him before they notice.
He'll be famous. Either in the arena or on your gravestone.
ROLL OF THE CENTURY. One in ten thousand and more. If he dies, your future dies with him.
Mars lost this one personally. He'll want him back.
You roll something like this once in a lifetime. Yours is in danger from now on; there are plenty of envious men.
Keep him away from the smith. And the medicus. And yourself.

karte.verdeckt: What he can really do only shows after the purchase.
karte.laedt: The trader is polishing his goods…

haendler.name: Gaius the Trader

1: {N}? Oh, him. I'd have given him to you for free. But you paid, so.
No returns. It's in the small print. I just forgot to show it to you.
Congratulations. You've just bought a mouth with legs.
If he dies, nobody will notice. That's a quality too.
He holds a sword like a child holds a spoon. The wrong way round.
Let's put it this way: as a target he's unbeatable.
A hundred gold for {N}. I was hoping for fifty. Thank you!
His mother wept when I took him. With relief.
He's good at standing in the way. That's worth something in the arena. To the opponent.
The lions will like the taste. That's all I'm promising.
I tried to get rid of him three times. You're the first to say yes.
Fighting spirit? He has it. Somewhere. Well hidden.
From behind he looks just as useless as from the front. I checked.
{N} is the reason wooden swords exist.
My condolences. I mean: congratulations.
He lost an arm-wrestle to my donkey. Twice.
As a doorstop I can recommend him at once.
You've got a good eye, Lanista. Just not today.
Feeding him barely pays. But that's your call.
I won't take him back. Not even for free. Better safe than sorry.
2: Well. He has two arms and two legs. That's about it.
{N} tries hard. You can see it. Sadly you can also see the result.
With a lot of training he might become a mediocre loser.
He needs three attempts to hit a door.
Good enough for the first round. For the second, more as a memory.
I said he's strong. I didn't say he knows what to do with it.
An honest lad. Honestly bad.
He doesn't trip often. Only when he moves.
Look at him: that's the face of a man who's about to lose.
A hundred gold is a hundred gold. For me, anyway.
{N} will surprise you. Mostly unpleasantly.
He isn't stupid. He just isn't particularly clever, strong or fast.
Give him a good sword. Then at least the sword looks good.
The arena sand can't wait. He'll see it up close a lot.
I've sold worse. Not many, but a few.
If he ever wins, buy a round. It'll be a party.
He has heart. It usually ends up lying next to him.
He has talent like a stone has wings.
He's worth gold for the laughs from the crowd. More than a hundred.
Train him hard. Or don't. Makes little difference.
3: Mediocre. Like the weather in Ostia: nobody talks about it.
{N} is neither good nor bad. More sort of… there.
Solid. Boring, but solid.
He'll never be famous. But he won't die on day one either. Probably.
The average has a face. It's his.
For a hundred gold, exactly what you'd expect for a hundred gold.
Not a bad buy. Not a lucky find. A buy.
He fills the ranks. Somebody has to stand at the back.
If he trains diligently, he'll become mediocre with a gold star.
The crowd won't love him. Won't boo him either. Mostly.
He has that look: half warrior, half farmer. Both halves tired.
A man for the second row. The third would be fine too.
Honest goods. I didn't even have to lie.
{N} does what he's told. No better, no worse.
You forget him quickly. So do his opponents.
More bread than circuses, this lad.
Expect nothing and you'll be pleasantly surprised. A little.
He's the bread among gladiators. Fills you up, excites nobody.
Not bad for a man without qualities.
I could have sold him as a talent. I'm feeling merciful today.
4: Usable. From me, that's a compliment.
{N} can do something. Not much, but something.
Good hands, good feet, mediocre head. Enough for the arena.
You can put him out there without being ashamed.
He can take a beating. He proved it on the journey.
A workhorse. No racehorse, but he pulls.
I saw him snap a chain. A small one.
A decent buy. I'm almost a bit annoyed.
With some polish he'll be really useful.
He'll get you a few wins. And a few scars.
For the price? Not bad, Lanista, not bad.
He has that sparkle in his eyes. Or fever. One of the two.
{N} fights until it hurts. Then he whines.
Put him up against someone better. He'll learn from it.
No hero, but he doesn't run away. That's rare enough.
Someone you can count on. Up to three at least.
Usable, to me, means he doesn't die immediately.
I should have asked two hundred. I'll remember that.
Not the crowd's darling. Maybe yours.
Decent goods. Almost too good for you.
5: Oh. He's actually gifted. Had I known…
{N} has talent. I never saw it in him.
Well, look at that, a gifted one. You're lucky, Lanista.
Train him two months and he'll be among the better ones.
With him the good food pays off.
I hate to say it: that was a good buy.
Gifted! And I sold him for a hundred. I'm getting old.
He knows which way is forward. That's more than many know.
Keep an eye on him. Ones like him get stolen fast.
The lad has fire. And plenty of room to grow.
{N} learns fast. Don't teach him too much or he'll run off.
Good choice. Really. I only lie sometimes.
With him you can show your face in the arena.
He has the hands of a fighter and the head of a survivor.
He's got something. I just don't know why I missed it.
A hundred gold for him? Don't tell anyone.
If you ever sell him, ask me first.
Gifted. I don't use that word often.
Give him time and he'll give you wins.
A hit, Lanista. Right in the gold.
6: By Jupiter, he's talented! I should have kept him.
{N}?! Give him back, I'll pay you a hundred and twenty!
Talented. I'm cursing my own price right now.
He'll make a name for himself. Hopefully not at my expense.
You've fleeced me, Lanista. Respect.
You don't find one like him every day. I certainly don't.
He has strength, brains and hunger. A dangerous mix.
The crowd will love him. And his opponents will fear him.
Don't tell anyone what you paid for him. My reputation!
I took him for a village idiot. I was the idiot.
{N} will be expensive. For your opponents.
Talent like his doesn't fall from the sky. He fell out of my cart.
Feed him well. And guard him even better.
With him you'll win fights you shouldn't win.
A lucky find. For you. For me, a mistake.
I'm going home now to reflect on my life.
Talented, you say? I say: too cheap!
He'll be a crowd favourite. Remember this day.
You don't sell one like him. You sell one like him by accident.
Make sure your smith doesn't grow too fond of him.
7: HIGHLY GIFTED?! That can't be. Show me again!
{N} is a jewel, and I sold him like a pebble.
The gods laughed today. At me.
Highly gifted. I think I need to sit down.
In a year Rome will cheer him. And I'll stand at the edge and weep.
For a hundred gold! My wife will kill me.
You have the eye of an eagle, Lanista. Or shameless luck.
One like him comes once a year. And today I gave him away.
I'll offer you two hundred. No? Three hundred? … Fine.
{N} will make history. With other men's blood.
Lock him up before someone buys him off you.
Highly gifted. I'm writing that down. As a warning to myself.
That's not a slave. That's a gold mine with legs.
I should have checked him. I never check. That changes now.
He has hands like a sculptor and blows like a hammer.
I think I just sold my retirement.
Don't show him to any other lanista. They'd envy you. I already do.
With him you can stage big fights. Very big ones.
Congratulations. Now go, before I change my mind.
A hundred gold… a hundred gold… A HUNDRED GOLD!
8: An exceptional talent. And I, the donkey, sell him for a hundred.
{N} will become a legend. And I'm the idiot in the footnote.
By all the gods, give him back! I'll throw in a horse!
I've seen something like this three times in twenty years. And today I gave it away.
Exceptional talent. I can already hear the crowd roar. And myself howl.
He has that certain something. And now I have that certain nothing.
If you ever sell him, you'll be rich. He just made me poor.
I feel sick. That was far too cheap.
Handle him like a raw egg. A raw egg that kills.
{N} strikes so fast you only feel the blow the next day.
My ancestors are ashamed of me right now.
You made the catch of your life today. I made the mistake of mine.
An exceptional talent! I should have seen it in his cheeky walk.
He'll end up in songs. I'll end up in jokes.
Give him the best weapons. He's earned them. I've earned nothing.
I'm going to sell myself now. Probably fetches more.
With him you'll win titles, Lanista. Titles!
Treat him well. Otherwise he'll treat you.
An exceptional talent for a hundred gold. Tell my competitors, then at least they'll laugh.
I need a wine. A big one.
9: ELITE?! No. No, no, no. Give him here!
{N} is elite. And I'm now officially the dumbest trader in Italy.
Senators buy ones like him. For thousands. You paid a hundred.
I almost left him in the river on the way. Lucky you, I didn't.
Elite talent. I'm shaking. With rage.
All of Rome will know him. And you along with him.
I'll give you five hundred. Right now. No? You cutthroat.
That's not a purchase. That's robbery with a receipt.
He has eyes like a wolf and arms like an ox.
{N} eats champions for breakfast. With bread.
My children will starve. Your gladiators will stop losing.
Elite. I should have weighed him in gold.
Careful he doesn't get famous too fast. The famous get cheeky.
From today I'm only selling goats. You can't go wrong with goats.
When he stands in the arena, you'll say: got him from the fool with the whip.
An elite talent for the price of a donkey. And I'm the donkey.
He'll get songs. Several. With a chorus.
Keep him away from wine and women and he'll be immortal. Almost.
I underestimated you, Lanista. And him.
I'm off to the temple to ask what I did wrong.
10: A PRODIGY?! By all the gods of Olympus! This cannot be true!
{N} is a miracle. And I sold a miracle for a hundred gold.
One like him is born every hundred years. And I SOLD him.
I'm about to faint. Catch me. No, catch him instead.
A prodigy. The emperor himself would bid for him.
I'm ruined. Not in the purse. In the soul.
They'll carve the name {N} in stone. Mine they'll write in the sand.
I'll offer you everything I have. The other four included. And my cart.
The gods sent him. And I flogged him off.
A prodigy! I'll tell my grandchildren about this. In tears.
He does with his left what others can't manage with both hands.
This is the end of my career and the start of his.
Treat him like a god. He'll behave like one anyway.
A hundred gold. For a demigod. I should have become a priest.
{N} will fill arenas. I'm going to fill my cup.
If you ever give him away, I'll hunt you to the ends of the earth.
I swapped him at the harbour for two sacks of flour. Two!
With him you won't need any other gladiators. Just coffins for the opponents.
A prodigy. I have to write this down, or nobody will believe me.
Go. Just go. I never want to see you again. Until tomorrow.

pitch: FIVE FRESH ONES! And this time four of them can even walk!
A hundred gold! Elsewhere that won't even buy you a decent donkey!
Look at those shoulders! Born for the sand!
I'm practically robbing myself! My children will starve!
Pure champion blood! Probably.
They still have their teeth! Almost all! What more do you want?
Every one a future crowd favourite. I have an eye for these things!
Fresh off the ship! Smell him! … No, better not.
A hundred each, and I'll throw in the chain. No. Not the chain.
Elsewhere you'd pay triple! Elsewhere they lie, you see!
Nobody's coughing! Since this morning!
Hand-picked! By me personally! In the dark, but hand-picked!
The Senate would envy me this stock, if it knew I existed!
Guarantee? Of course! Up to the gate!
I've sold to emperors! Well… to a cousin. Of a cook.
Grab one before the competition wakes up!
Each one eats little and complains quietly. Dream goods!
Whoever doesn't buy today weeps in the arena tomorrow!
Death is only this cheap in a war!
You recognise quality by its price. A hundred gold. So: top quality!
All healthy! I asked them myself!
I'm the best judge of men in the empire. Ask anyone I pay!
Five of them! Take all five and you get my sincere smile on top!
They walk by themselves! Mostly in the right direction!
Barely used! Previous owner sadly deceased. Different matter entirely.
With me you buy a future! Sometimes a short one, but a future!
Did I mention my discount? There isn't one!
Look at those calves. They'll carry you all the way to the capital!
My goods only ever die after the sale!
A hundred gold. I haven't been this honest all week!
sold: Sold! Chain off! Run, boy, before he changes his mind!
HA! A connoisseur! He'll bring you joy. Or a funeral.
A hundred gold! Hear that jingle? That's music!
Good choice! I say that every time, but this time I almost mean it!
Off to the barracks with you! And don't disgrace me!
A deal between men of honour! Count it if you like, I will.
He's yours now! The fleas too!
Sold! Next, please, the chain's getting lighter!
That's how business is done! Quick, before anyone thinks!
empty: HAHA! Finally someone with taste! Tomorrow I'll bring you five new ones!
Sold out! I love this ludus! Until tomorrow, my friend!
All five! You're my favourite person! Tomorrow again, same time!
Empty chain, full purse. That's how I like it! Until tomorrow!
broke: No gold? Then stop looking at my goods so hungrily!
Without gold you're air to me. Bad air!
A hundred gold or move along. I only give credit to the dead!
Your purse sounds like my conscience: empty!

tactics: Doesn't think much. An excellent quality in a fighter!
He doesn't brood, he hits. Usually the right way round!
strength: Weak? He's just saving his strength!
Not strong, but easy to carry when it goes wrong!
stamina: Fights briefly. Saves the spectators time!
Quickly out of breath. At least the fights are over fast!
condition: Wheezes a bit. That intimidates opponents!
agility: Barely moves. A rock in the surf!
dexterity: Two left hands. Twice as many left hooks!
reflex: Reacts late. But nothing surprises him for long!
Can't be rushed. A man at peace!
precision: Rarely hits. The opponent never knows where he's aiming!
block: Doesn't need a shield. Saves you money!
balance: Falls over easily. Nobody hits him in the head down there!
pain: Screams loudly. The crowd loves emotion!
will: Gives up quickly. Lives longer that way. Clever boy!
aggression: Peaceable. At least he won't start fights in the barracks!
teamwork: A loner. Shares the glory with no one!
experience: Learns slowly. But he forgets nothing either, because he knows nothing!

thin: Thin as a spear. And a spear is a weapon!
fat: That's not fat, that's armour on the inside!
Supplies for the winter, all included!
small: The little one? Don't underestimate him. He's survived three men. How, I won't say.
tall: You'll see him from the last row! The spectators will thank you!
Tall as a watchtower. Falls like one too, just later!
old: A mature vintage! Experience can't be bought. Yes it can. Here. For a hundred.
Old? He's outlived everyone who was younger!
young: Young and malleable! Has no ideas of his own yet!
Fresh as blood! Lasts forever! Probably.
weak: A blank parchment! That's exactly what you're paying for!
Can't do anything yet. So he can't do anything wrong!
Raw as fresh marble. You're the sculptor!

Feige: Knows exactly when to run. A survival artist!
Egoistisch: Thinks of himself first. So of your property!
Verletzungsanfällig: He'll soon know every medicus by first name. Connections are everything!
Berserker: Bites. But only if you look at him!
Blutrünstig: Enjoys his work. Rare these days!
Aggressiv: Temperament! You don't need to fire him up, just let him go!
Gelassen: Calm itself. Even slept through the crossing!
Mutig: Brave! Contradicted me twice. Still alive!
Loyal: Loyal as a dog. Eats like one too!
Diszipliniert: Stands to attention as soon as someone coughs!
Taktiker: A thinker! Tried to open the chain three times. Almost managed!
Teamspieler: Gets on with everyone. Even with me!
Zäh: Tough as old leather. Probably tastes like it too!
Schneller Lerner: Learns fast! Knew all my curses after one day!

gem: That one? Er. Nothing special. Really not. A hundred gold, quick, before I think about it!
Hm. I actually wanted to keep that one myself. … A hundred. But NOW!
Don't stare at him like that! He's a perfectly ordinary… ahem… A hundred gold, like all of them!
My nose itches with that one. It only itches for gold. Take him before I double the price!
I should ask a thousand. I SHOULD ask a thousand! … A hundred. I hate myself.
jewel: BY ALL THE GODS, not so loud! That one is… whatever. A hundred. My hands are only shaking from the weather!
I promised him to a king! Two kings! A hundred gold and you never saw me!
Look away! No, look! No… a hundred gold, and I'll weep into my purse tonight!

dwarf: Small, I know. But look at those arms! He lifts more than you do.
The crowd will love him. Small and furious; there's no better spectacle for a hundred gold.
Don't underestimate him. Plenty have. They're under the ground now; he's still standing.
He comes up to your belt and still lifts you off the ground.
In Ostia they paid double admission for him. Double, Lanista!
giant: A giant! No joke, look up. Further. Further still.
I needed three chains to bring him. He snapped one on the way.
Slow, yes. But when he hits, nobody gets up. Give him something two-handed.
The crowd will go wild. The crowd always goes wild for a giant. Double prize money, if you ask me.
He eats for three. He fights for three too.
sumo: Yes, he's heavy. Very heavy. My cart lost two axles. But knock him over? Nobody knocks him over.
He'll eat your stores bare, I warn you. In return swords bounce off him like off a wine barrel.
He isn't fast. He doesn't need to be fast. He just needs to stand there.
A rock in human form. Whoever runs at him runs into a wall.
People laugh when he comes in. When he leaves, nobody's laughing.
